title: web_test.rs is load-sensitively flaky: wait_for_server races the server readiness handshake

description:
## What

`tests/web_test.rs` fails nondeterministically, swinging between 0 and 60 failures across consecutive runs on a byte-identical tree. Observed counts in one sitting: 0, 27, 57, 2, 44, 0, 0, 60, 0, 0.

Nearly every failure is a spurious `404` — e.g. `web_serve_get_story_by_id` (line 994) panicking on `Err value: StatusCode(404)`, `web_reopen_malformed_json_is_400` (line 1715) asserting `left: 404, right: 400`.

## Why it breaks

`wait_for_server` (tests/web_test.rs:3616) only polls until the TCP port accepts a connection:

    if std::net::TcpStream::connect(addr).is_ok() { return; }

But `storyhook::web::start_server` does not finish loading registry/project state until its filesystem watcher completes the `watcher_ready_rx` handshake (see `web.rs`). The listener therefore accepts connections before the server can resolve `/api/repos/<id>/...`, and any request that wins that race gets a 404 from a server that is listening but not yet ready.

`wait_for_addr` documents awareness of exactly this hazard for the *tailnet* listener, but `wait_for_server` — used by the bulk of the suite for the loopback listener — still gates on `connect()` alone.

## Extent

Load-sensitive, which is why it looks random. It correlates with `fseventsd` CPU: the readiness handshake is FSEvents-backed, so anything keeping the filesystem-events daemon busy widens the window. Reproduced with load average ~5.5.

Amplified severely on macOS by a missing `$TMPDIR/.metadata_never_index` marker (see sibling story) — with Spotlight indexing the suite fixtures, failures hit 57/123; restoring the marker dropped the same suite to 0-2.

## Repro

    for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do cargo test --test web_test 2>&1 | tail -3; done

under moderate system load. Expect at least one run with a large block of 404 failures.

## Last known good

Never reliably good; the race is inherent to the readiness probe. Surfaced during the v0.17.0 release (PR #51), which touches no Rust source.

## Fix

Gate the probe on real readiness rather than on `connect()` succeeding — poll an actual endpoint (e.g. `/api/repos/<id>/...` or a dedicated health route) until it returns non-404, with the existing 5s deadline. A test that cannot distinguish "port open" from "server ready" will keep reintroducing this class, so the preventative action is to make the ready-probe helper the only sanctioned way tests wait for a server.

text: [git] e35a433: chore(storyhook): track SH-51, SH-52, SH-53

Fixed in commit 4c1aed9, with a follow-on production fix in e8d4cf8 (branch rearch/w0-gate-repair, W0.1). The mechanism proven on 2026-07-28 was not the readiness race in the description but orphaned web_test processes from earlier runs holding ~100 LISTEN sockets across 19000-19095: a fresh run restarted the fixed PORT_COUNTER at 19000, collided, and because start_server's error was swallowed with .ok() and readiness was 'the port accepts a connection', the suite talked to the ORPHAN's stale registry - 78/139 failures, all spurious 404s. Three fixes, one per link: (a) start_server_with_ready reports the address the loopback listener actually got, so in-process test servers bind port 0 and are told their port - collision is impossible, not unlikely; the four tests that must know a port before the process binding it exists draw from a randomized bind-tested band outside the ephemeral range. (b) serve/try_serve_on wait for the server's own ready callback (fired after the watcher handshake) and never swallow a start-up failure; connect_sse grew a deadline, having previously retried forever against a bound-but-silent listener while holding the SSE lock. (c) DaemonGuard stops a test-launched daemon even on panic, and make test brackets the run with scripts/check-no-orphan-servers.sh, which names surviving pids from this worktree (never the installed :3456 daemon). Regression tests: serving_an_occupied_port_fails_loudly_instead_of_trusting_the_squatter (red: reported the squatter's port as ready; green: reports 'in use') and concurrent_servers_get_distinct_ports_and_serve_only_their_own_registry. THEN, with real readiness in place, ~1 run in 5 failed with 'neither became ready nor reported a failure within 10s': tailnet_identity shells out to tailscale status --json with an unbounded Command::output(), after the loopback listener is bound - and tailscaled wedges (probes found stuck for minutes, orphaned by exited servers). That is the description's original hypothesis (listener accepting before it can serve), proven, and it hits production too: story web start's daemon would sit on :3456 listening and permanently silent. e8d4cf8 bounds the probe to 3s, kills its process group on overrun and serves localhost only; regression test a_wedged_tailscale_cli_cannot_stop_the_dashboard_from_serving puts a hanging fake tailscale ahead of the real one on PATH (red: never served; green: 3.8s). web_test 143/143 across repeated runs. That production defect deserves its own story - not filed from this worktree because minting an id here would collide with ids being minted in parallel worktrees.
